title: Register of Refusal Grounds and Appeals — Northbeam Returns and Restocking
content:
### Grounds on which a return is refused at the request

A return on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking schedule is refused at the request where the line is final sale, where the window has run out, or where the customer cannot produce the proof of purchase a schedule requires and none is on file.

### Grounds on which a return is refused after inspection

A return is refused after inspection where the serial does not match what was sold, where the item is not the item described on the authorisation, or where the item was never the retailer's merchandise.

### What a refusal must name, and what follows it

A refusal names the ground it rests on and the grade it rests on where the item was inspected, and the item is sent back to the customer at the retailer's cost when the refusal follows an inspection. The customer may appeal inside the schedule's appeal window and the appeal is decided on the same authorisation; a second refusal on the same ground closes the matter. A return is never refused because the profile has returned a great deal: that is a matter for review, and the review governs the refund method rather than the right to return.

### The register in one view

| Ground | Refused at | The item |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the line is final sale | the request | stays with the customer |
| the window has run out | the request | stays with the customer |
| the proof of purchase a schedule requires cannot be produced and none is on file | the request | stays with the customer |
| the serial does not match what was sold | after inspection | sent back to the customer at the retailer's cost |
| the item is not the item described on the authorisation | after inspection | sent back to the customer at the retailer's cost |
| the item was never the retailer's merchandise | after inspection | sent back to the customer at the retailer's cost |

### Points of judgement

**A refusal after an inspection names two things.** The ground, and the grade the refusal rests on.

**An appeal does not open a new return.** It is decided on the same authorisation, inside the schedule's appeal window.

**A second refusal on the same ground closes the matter.**

**A heavy return history is not a ground of refusal.** It is a matter for review, and the review governs the refund method rather than the right to return.
